title: "Cross Validation"
output: github_document

```{r message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(p8105.datasets)
library(modelr)
library(mgcv)
```

* In model fitting, we want consistent predictions but nothing too simple - something medium complexity is important for the best prediction accuracy. 

* Random split data into training data (build model) and testing data (out of sample fit). Can be around 80/20 ratio (use root mean squared error to measure).

* So in general, helps you choose between models of varying complexity. Can be built into programs.

## LIDAR Data 

```{r}
data("lidar")

lidar_df =
  lidar |>
  mutate(id = row_number()) |>
  select(id, everything())

lidar_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = range, y = logratio)) +
  geom_point()
```

Mutate added the new column named `id` with values that are the row numbers. `select` changes order so `id` is first from the left in the df.

Build training and testing datasets.

```{r}
train_df = sample_frac(lidar_df, size = 0.8)
test_df = anti_join(lidar_df, train_df, by = "id")
```

`size = 0.8` is the 80% fraction of the data that we're sampling. `test_df` term removes everything not in `train_df`. 

```{r}
ggplot(train_df, aes(x = range, y = logratio)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_point(data = test_df, color = "red")
```

Overlaying the two datasets, training versus testing distinction.

Fit some models.

```{r}
linear_mod = lm(logratio ~ range, data = train_df)
smooth_mod = gam(logratio ~ s(range), data = train_df)
wiggly_mod = gam(logratio ~ s(range,  k = 30), sp = 10e-6, data = train_df)
```

Make a plot

```{r}
train_df |>
  add_predictions(wiggly_mod) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = range, y = logratio)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(aes(y = pred), color = "red")
```

Adding predictions (fitted values) from linear model to training df and then adding linear fit line/smooth model fit line. 

Do a model comparison!

```{r}
rmse(linear_mod, test_df)
rmse(smooth_mod, test_df)
rmse(wiggly_mod, test_df)
```

* Lower `rmse` returned are better fit

## Repeat a bunch of times

Use some nice tools woo

```{r}
cv_df =
  crossv_mc(lidar_df, 100)

cv_df |> pull(train) |> nth(2) |> as_tibble()
```

```{r}
cv_df = 
  crossv_mc(lidar_df, 100) |>
  mutate(
    train = map(train, as_tibble),
    test = map(test, as_tibble)
  )
```

Fitting models and get rmses for these.

```{r}
rmse_comp = function(model, dataset) {
  
  rmse(model, dataset)
  
}
```

```{r}
cv_df = 
  cv_df |>
  mutate(
    linear_fit = map(train, \(df) lm(logratio ~ range, data = df)),
    smooth_fit = map(train, \(df) gam(logratio ~ s(range), data = df)),
    wiggly_fit = map(train, \(df) gam(logratio ~ s(range, k = 30), sp = 10e-6, data = df))
  ) |>
  mutate(
    rmse_linear = map2_dbl(linear_fit, test, rmse),
    rmse_smooth = map2_dbl(smooth_fit, test, rmse),
    rmse_wiggly = map2_dbl(wiggly_fit, test, rmse)
  )
```

* Figure out what an anonymous function is (`\(df)`)

Look at this!

```{r}
cv_df |>
  select(starts_with("rmse_")) |>
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "model",
    names_prefix = "rmse_",
    values_to = "rmse"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = model, y = rmse)) +
  geom_violin()
```

## Child growth

```{r}
growth_df =
  read_csv("data/nepalese_children.csv") |>
  mutate(
    weight_ch7 = (weight > 7) * (weight - 7)
  )
```

Look at this

```{r}
growth_df

growth_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = weight, y = armc)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5)
```

```{r}
linear_fit = lm(armc ~ weight, data = growth_df)
pwl_fit = lm(armc ~ weight + weight_ch7, data = growth_df)
smooth_fit = gam(armc ~ s(weight), data = growth_df)
```

```{r}
growth_df |>
  add_predictions(pwl_fit) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = weight, y = armc)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(aes(y = pred), color = "red")
```

Doing all cross validation stuff we know and love.
